channel.title: T47 Group — Insights
channel.description: Building, operating, and investing across technology, staffing, and consumer products — from Phoenix, Arizona.

item.title: Knowing when to kill a venture
item.description: Persistence is celebrated and quitting isn't, which is why most founders hold on too long. Here's how I try to tell the difference.

item.title: Hiring your first real operator
item.description: The hardest hire isn't a specialist. It's the person who takes an entire piece of the business off your desk — and most founders get it wrong the same way.

item.title: Phoenix is an underrated place to build a company
item.description: I've built here for twenty years. The advantages are real, and so are two disadvantages nobody local wants to say out loud.

item.title: Let the boring business fund the interesting one
item.description: Everyone wants to build the ambitious thing. Almost nobody wants to own the unglamorous business that makes building it possible without permission.

item.title: Shared services: the actual advantage of a portfolio
item.description: Holding companies justify themselves with synergy and rarely deliver it. Here's what actually shares across ventures — and what stubbornly doesn't.

item.title: How we decide what to build next
item.description: Everyone has more ideas than capacity. Here are the four filters we run a new venture through before it gets a dollar or a developer.

item.title: What a staffing business taught me about software margins
item.description: Labor businesses teach you things software founders learn late and expensively. The most useful lesson is that gross margin is a habit, not a number.

item.title: Why we hold companies instead of flipping them
item.description: The exit is the default goal in almost every founder conversation. After twenty years of building, I think it's the wrong default for most businesses.
